sections.instruction: Use a suitable present or past MODAL AUXILIARY:

questions.prompt: I can’t find my book. I [gap] (leave) it on the bus.
acceptedAnswers: must have left|may have left|might have left|could have left
questions.explanation: must/may have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: They don’t answer their phone; they [gap] (go) away on their vacation.
acceptedAnswers: must have gone|may have gone|might have gone|could have gone
questions.explanation: must/may have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: John went to the movies last night, but he [gap] (stay) at home and [gap] (prepare) his lessons.
acceptedAnswers: should have stayed|ought to have stayed / prepared|should have prepared|ought to have prepared
questions.explanation: should have + V3: criticism of a past action

questions.prompt: The lights have gone out. A fuse [gap] (blow).
acceptedAnswers: must have blown|may have blown|might have blown|could have blown
questions.explanation: must have + V3: logical conclusion about the past

questions.prompt: She [gap] (go) to school. It’s Saturday.
acceptedAnswers: doesn't have to go|needn't go|need not go|doesn't need to go|can't be going|won't go
questions.explanation: doesn't have to / needn't: no obligation

questions.prompt: You were stupid to go skiing here. You [gap] (break) your leg.
acceptedAnswers: could have broken|might have broken|may have broken
questions.explanation: could/might have + V3: past possibility that didn't happen

questions.prompt: She [gap] (sing) like an angel when she was a kid.
acceptedAnswers: could sing|used to sing

questions.prompt: [gap] I make a suggestion?
acceptedAnswers: may|can|could|might

questions.prompt: You [gap] go and see “Batman”. It’s a great film.
acceptedAnswers: should|must|ought to

questions.prompt: He came home alone. You [gap] (let) him do that; he [gap] (get) lost.
acceptedAnswers: shouldn't have let|ought not to have let|oughtn't to have let / might have got|could have got|may have got|might have gotten|could have gotten|may have gotten
questions.explanation: shouldn't have + V3: criticism; might have + V3: possibility

questions.prompt: He read the message but he [gap] (not) understand.
acceptedAnswers: couldn't|didn't

questions.prompt: I [gap] (lend) you the money. Why didn’t you ask me?
acceptedAnswers: could have lent|would have lent
questions.explanation: could have + V3: possible but didn't happen

questions.prompt: A: Can I have some sweets? I am hungry. B: You [gap] hungry. You have just had dinner.
acceptedAnswers: can't be|couldn't be

questions.prompt: Tom [gap] (write) this, because it is in French and he doesn’t know French.
acceptedAnswers: can't have written|couldn't have written
questions.explanation: can't have + V3: negative deduction about the past

questions.prompt: He looked so tired. He [gap] (work) very hard.
acceptedAnswers: must have worked|must have been working
questions.explanation: must have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: He [gap] be a very clever boy. He has entered the university very easily.
acceptedAnswers: must

sections.instruction: Fill in the blanks using MUST, CAN’T, MAY, MIGHT, COULD and PAST FORMS of them:

questions.prompt: Sally looks sad and worried. She [gap] (have) a problem with something.
acceptedAnswers: must have|may have|might have|could have

questions.prompt: Bob [gap] (be) at school because I haven’t seen him today.
acceptedAnswers: can't be|can't have been|couldn't have been|couldn't be

questions.prompt: Mr. Treves hasn’t come to work yet. He has never been late for work. He [gap] (miss) the bus.
acceptedAnswers: must have missed|may have missed|might have missed|could have missed
questions.explanation: must/may have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: Timmy is a very good boy. He isn’t naughty, so he [gap] (break) that window. Someone else [gap] (break) it.
acceptedAnswers: can't have broken|couldn't have broken / must have broken
questions.explanation: can't have / must have + V3: past deduction

questions.prompt: I’m sure that I dropped my key in the car. It [gap] (be) there at the moment.
acceptedAnswers: must be

questions.prompt: The street is wet this morning. I’m not sure but it [gap] (rain) last night.
acceptedAnswers: may have rained|might have rained|could have rained
questions.explanation: may/might have + V3: uncertain past possibility

questions.prompt: A: I talked to your science teacher at school yesterday. B: You [gap] (talk) to her because she wasn’t at school yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: can't have talked|couldn't have talked
questions.explanation: can't have + V3: negative past deduction

questions.prompt: A: The man was being taken to hospital. He [gap] (have) an accident. B: Yes, I’m sure he had an accident.
acceptedAnswers: must have had
questions.explanation: must have + V3: sure about the past

questions.prompt: A: Will you come to my birthday party tomorrow? B: I [gap] (come) to your party because I have to look after my little sister.
acceptedAnswers: can't come|won't be able to come

questions.prompt: A: I’m going to do a parachute jump next week. B: You are going to jump out of an aeroplane! But you’re 73 years old! You [gap] (be) serious. You [gap] (be) mad.
acceptedAnswers: can't be / must be

questions.prompt: A: It really [gap] (be) wonderful looking down on everything. I’ve always wanted to try it.
acceptedAnswers: must be

questions.prompt: B: But anything could happen. You [gap] (be) injured, or even killed. I wouldn’t take the risk.
acceptedAnswers: could be|might be|may be

questions.prompt: A: Well, your life [gap] (be) much fun if you never take risks. You ought to try it, too. You never know. You [gap] (enjoy) it.
acceptedAnswers: can't be|couldn't be / might enjoy|may enjoy|could enjoy

questions.prompt: B: Enjoy it! You [gap] (be) joking.
acceptedAnswers: must be

questions.prompt: She knew everything about our plans. She [gap] (listen) to our conversation.
acceptedAnswers: must have listened|must have been listening
questions.explanation: must have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: He [gap] (eat) the roasted beef when we were out. He is a vegetarian.
acceptedAnswers: can't have eaten|couldn't have eaten
questions.explanation: can't have + V3: negative past deduction

questions.prompt: Mrs. White bought a new fur coat! She [gap] (win) a lottery.
acceptedAnswers: must have won|may have won|might have won
questions.explanation: must/may have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: John said he would ring, but he hasn’t. He [gap] (forget) all about it.
acceptedAnswers: must have forgotten|may have forgotten|might have forgotten
questions.explanation: must/may have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: The children [gap] (study) in the library now because they have a test tomorrow.
acceptedAnswers: must be studying|may be studying|might be studying

questions.prompt: The singer has got a sore throat, so she [gap] (sing) at the concert.
acceptedAnswers: can't sing|won't be able to sing|may not sing|might not sing

questions.prompt: I [gap] (be) at home this evening, or I [gap] (be) out, I’m not sure.
acceptedAnswers: may be|might be|could be / may be|might be|could be

questions.prompt: He drank three glasses of water. He [gap] (be) very thirsty.
acceptedAnswers: must have been
questions.explanation: must have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: A: Where’s the cat? B: It [gap] (go) out, the door is closed.
acceptedAnswers: can't have gone|couldn't have gone
questions.explanation: can't have + V3: negative past deduction

questions.prompt: The police arrested him right away. They [gap] (find) enough evidence.
acceptedAnswers: must have found
questions.explanation: must have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: He had no money, so he [gap] (lend) you some.
acceptedAnswers: can't have lent|couldn't have lent
questions.explanation: can't have + V3: negative past deduction

questions.prompt: We can’t wait any longer. Something [gap] (do) immediately.
acceptedAnswers: must be done

questions.prompt: They all shouted in fear. They [gap] (be) very afraid.
acceptedAnswers: must have been
questions.explanation: must have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: A: Your dog bit me as I was standing in the hall. B: It [gap] (be) my dog. It was with me all day.
acceptedAnswers: can't have been|couldn't have been
questions.explanation: can't have + V3: negative past deduction

questions.prompt: A: I phoned you at 9 o’clock this morning and got no answer. B: I [gap] (be) in the garden. I planted some flowers this morning.
acceptedAnswers: must have been
questions.explanation: must have + V3: deduction about the past

questions.prompt: My grandmother always has a rest at this time of the day, so she [gap] (take) a nap now.
acceptedAnswers: must be taking

questions.prompt: Mrs. Green wasn’t good at ice-skating, but she insisted on and broke her leg. She [gap] (give) up doing that.
acceptedAnswers: should have given|ought to have given
questions.explanation: should have + V3: criticism of a past action

questions.prompt: A: I’m afraid Ted is watching TV again. B: He [gap] (watch) TV, because his room is completely silent and dark. He [gap] (sleep).
acceptedAnswers: can't be watching|couldn't be watching / must be sleeping
questions.explanation: can't / must be + -ing: deduction about now

questions.prompt: That carpet was made by hand. It [gap] (take) a long time to make it.
acceptedAnswers: must have taken
questions.explanation: must have + V3: deduction about the past

sections.instruction: Decide what you MUST, MUSTN’T or NEEDN’T do and then write them down as in the examples: (Examples: tidy your room → I must tidy my room. / cheat on the exams → I mustn’t cheat on the exams.)

questions.prompt: do your homework regularly
acceptedAnswers: I must do my homework regularly.

questions.prompt: listen to the teacher
acceptedAnswers: I must listen to the teacher.

questions.prompt: visit the teacher
acceptedAnswers: I needn't visit the teacher.
I need not visit the teacher.
I don't need to visit the teacher.
I don't have to visit the teacher.

questions.prompt: run in the halls
acceptedAnswers: I mustn't run in the halls.
I must not run in the halls.

questions.prompt: talk during the test
acceptedAnswers: I mustn't talk during the test.
I must not talk during the test.

questions.prompt: wake up early at weekends
acceptedAnswers: I needn't wake up early at weekends.
I need not wake up early at weekends.
I don't need to wake up early at weekends.
I don't have to wake up early at weekends.

questions.prompt: get to class late
acceptedAnswers: I mustn't get to class late.
I must not get to class late.

questions.prompt: wash your hands before meals
acceptedAnswers: I must wash my hands before meals.
I must wash my hands before a meal.
I must wash my hands before each meal.
I must wash my hand before meal.

questions.prompt: wear a tie at parties
acceptedAnswers: I needn't wear a tie at parties.
I need not wear a tie at parties.
I needn't wear a tie at the parties.
I don't have to wear a tie at parties.

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences with MUST / MUSTN’T or NEEDN’T: (Examples: I haven’t got much time. I must hurry. / I have got plenty of time. I needn’t hurry.)

questions.prompt: “Do you want me to wait for you?” “No, it’s okay. You [gap] wait.”
acceptedAnswers: needn't|need not

questions.prompt: Smith gave me a letter to post. I [gap] forget to post it.
acceptedAnswers: mustn't|must not

questions.prompt: You [gap] come if you don’t want to but I hope you will.
acceptedAnswers: needn't|need not

questions.prompt: We have enough food at home so we [gap] go shopping today.
acceptedAnswers: needn't|need not

questions.prompt: This book is very valuable. You [gap] look after it very carefully and you [gap] lose it.
acceptedAnswers: must / mustn't|must not

questions.prompt: You have got a new skirt, so you [gap] buy another.
acceptedAnswers: needn't|need not

questions.prompt: It’s holiday tomorrow. You [gap] get up early.
acceptedAnswers: needn't|need not

questions.prompt: He’s ill, so he [gap] see the doctor.
acceptedAnswers: must

questions.prompt: It’s snowing. You [gap] put on your coat.
acceptedAnswers: must

questions.prompt: You [gap] take too many aspirins in one day.
acceptedAnswers: mustn't|must not
